text:
mari: Ran a perfetto capture against a steady-state load (50k requests over 10m) to investigate a recurring 60-120ms tail spike. Trace here: https://perfetto.app/trace/ABC123 :eyes:
aj: link opens, thanks. Quick q: which scenario? single-token chat or long-seq generation? :thinking:
mari: long-seq (avg 256, p95 512). Client -> gateway -> runtime spans show a 40-90ms gap between gateway send and runtime recv in the bad cases. It's not pure GPU compute.
kevin: can you paste the timestamp window (ns) or a short perfetto slice? want to check kernel handoff and any NVTX marks for kv cache.
mari: slice around 00:04:12. See span timeline snippet:
```
perfetto://trace#time=00:04:12-00:04:13
client_send -> gateway_recv 1.2ms
gateway_process 14.8ms
gateway_send 0.6ms
<idle gap> 62.5ms
runtime_recv 0.9ms
runtime_kernel_select 0.3ms
kv_cache_lookup 0.7ms
attn_fwd_fp16 11.2ms
```
mari: note the <idle gap> between gateway_send and runtime_recv is where requests are queuing at gateway or RPC layer.
perf-bot: nsys capture automated at 1766504330 for runtime pod-3 uploaded to S3 (s3://redwood-traces/nsys/1766504330.nsight).
aj: what's the kernel_select composition? is it re-compiling or switching quantized kernels? any stalls waiting on device memory?
mari: kernel_select resolves to kernel variant map quickly (0.3ms) but we see a repeated pattern where kv_cache_lookup misses 40% of time, which triggers a small CPU fetch from the parameter server and introduces the 60ms gap when combined with gateway batching. nvprof/nsys shows CPU-side memcpy + socket read waiting ~55ms in those traces.
kevin: that smells like batching heuristic interaction: gateway waits for batch fill (batching threshold 8 or 4ms), then sends a single RPC for the batch. If kv miss on one request, the whole batch waits for PS response serially. Can we repro with forced kv miss rate?
sam: repro plan: (1) run load with synthetic kv miss toggled (2) run perfetto and nsys simultaneously (3) flip gateway batching-policy to latency-first (ms threshold -> 2ms) and compare end-to-end p99. I can spin up the test harness.
mari: commands used to capture (FYI):
```
# run perfetto trace (local dev)
perfetto --out trace.pb --duration=600 --config perfetto_cfg.pbtxt
# start load
wrk2 -t16 -c200 -d600s -R5000 --latency http://gateway-host/generate
# start nsys on runtime (container)
nsys profile --output=nsys_1766504330 --trace=nvtx,cuda python3 runtime_server.py
```
aj: good. also add a short logging patch at gateway to emit batch size and per-item kv-hit flags (json list). we need to know if misses correlate with specific clients/paths.
kevin: another hypothesis: batching window + RPC serialization order causes head-of-batch request to miss kv, then runtime processes sequentially blocking other items. if runtime could parallelize kv fetch or prefetch hot keys, we might avoid the tail.
mari: observed that when kv_cache_hit_rate > 0.9, tail spikes disappear. With current workload we saw 0.58 hit rate. Prefetching hot prefixes helped in a quick local test.
perf-bot: Note: previous deploy 1766490000 rolled out kernel-selection micro-optimization; no changes to kv code.
sam: ok I'll run controlled experiments with three configs: baseline, low-latency gateway batching, and aggressive prefetch on runtime. Will attach perfetto links. Timeline: run today, results by EOD.
aj: assign follow-ups: mari -> collect a set of perfetto windows where gap >50ms, export as short traces; kevin -> prototype simple async kv-fetch in runtime (non-blocking per-request); sam -> run A/B tests with gateway batching-policy.
mari: uploaded 6 short perfetto slices to https://perfetto.app/trace/ABC123 (ids slice1..slice6). Pls check slice3 - it's the cleanest repro.
kevin: thanks. if sam sees improvement with latency-first batching, we might change default to lower threshold and add an adaptive mode based on kv_hotness metric.
aj: fine. also add low-cost metric: per-batch kv_miss_ratio exported to console dashboard. we can alert when >0.2.
mari: noted. I'll open a PR for gateway logging and add the perfetto slices to the ticket.
sam: ping when slices are uploaded to the infra job so I can run the nsys/NVTX matching.
mari: done — slices and nsys artifacts in the ticket (INF-4521).
kevin: ack. thanks all :thumbsup:
